chapter: Decca years and the First Herd
title: Early sidemen and arrangers: Bishop, Jenkins, Noble, Harper
summary: He names the first band's rhythm section, Joe Bishop's writing, and outside arrangers Gordon Jenkins, James Noble and Nick Harper.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: Who were some of the people who contributed significantly to that period?

Well, the early period, of course, would have to include people like Frankie Carlson, a drummer who did a good job for us, Tommy Linehan, a pianist, Walt Yoder, the bassist. Everyone was important in that first band, as far as what they were producing. Joe Bishop, of course, did a masterful job of writing tunes for the band, writing arrangements for the band, and then switching over from tuba, which he played with Isham, to flugelhorn with our band.
And then, we had a lot of outside contributors,

well, people who were really not outside, because Cordon Jenkins, for instance, who had been arranging for the Jones band when we were with him contributed because he knew we didn't have any bread, wrote some things for us, and this helped us. And a lot of good writers -- and James Noble wrote for the band for quite a while, and later, Nick Harper -- Harper is his original name -- a fiddle player. He wrote a lot of music for the band, and a lot of it was very different. He wrote a swinging arrangement of Meditation from Pais. And he wrote the melody line, and the band was shouting in back of him and you could never find him. And he loved it.
Were you in some way pulling things together from the variety of contributors to fit the direction that you had? Did you edit things then?
